findings.title: allocate_storage never persists zone.current_usage — unlimited overfill + false empty utilization
findings.description: StorageOptimizer.allocate_storage copies SiteZone.current_usage into a local zone_usage dict, increments only that local dict, and never writes back to zone.current_usage. get_storage_utilization reads zone.current_usage, so every batch restarts from 0 used. Distinct from already-reported crane-schedule soft check.
findings.impact: Contractor/logistics caller can assign multiples of laydown capacity (e.g. 300 TON into 100 TON zone). Utilization reports stay 0%/normal, hiding overload that drives congestion, unsafe stacking, and false capacity for deliveries.
attack_path: 3) Call allocate_storage again with M2 quantity=100 — assigned again because current_usage still 0
4) Repeat; get_storage_utilization shows used=0, utilization_pct=0, status=normal
findings.remediation: After allocation, persist zone.current_usage += quantity (and store assignments). Reject materials when zone.current_usage + quantity > capacity. Make get_storage_utilization derive used from persisted usage or assignments.

findings.title: Out-of-range readings marked SUSPECT skip all threshold alerts
findings.description: ingest_reading validates quality via min/max; values outside physical limits become DataQuality.SUSPECT. Threshold/critical checks run only when quality == GOOD. Beyond already-reported empty-default thresholds: extreme dangerous readings above max suppress safety alerts entirely.
findings.impact: Compromised or malicious sensor feed can push lethal/out-of-range gas, temperature, or structural values that never create WARNING/CRITICAL alerts — the worst readings are the ones silenced.
attack_path: 1) Register sensor with thresholds {min:0, max:100, warning:25, critical:50}
3) Ingest value=500 (> max) → SUSPECT → _check_thresholds skipped → alerts stay empty
findings.remediation: Always evaluate warning/critical thresholds regardless of quality; treat SUSPECT as an additional alert class; do not let max-bound failure suppress exceedance detection.

findings.title: WARNING alert blocks THRESHOLD_EXCEEDANCE for one hour
findings.description: _create_alert returns early if any unresolved alert for the same station/parameter exists within 3600s — including WARNING. A reading at ≥80% of limit creates WARNING; a later hard exceedance is dropped. Distinct from already-reported TWA averaging gaps.
findings.impact: Attacker or noisy sensor can seed a warning-level reading, then OSHA/ISO hard exceedances within the hour produce no EXCEEDANCE alert — compliance dashboards understate regulatory breach.
attack_path: 1) record_reading noise=70 on 85 dBA instantaneous limit (≥80% → WARNING)
3) recent_alerts gate returns; alerts list still only WARNING at 70
findings.remediation: Allow severity escalation (WARNING→EXCEEDANCE); key dedupe on alert_type+severity; never let a weaker alert suppress a stronger one.

findings.title: add_staff accepts unbounded capacity — forge GO on can_pursue_project
findings.description: add_staff stores attacker-controlled capacity with no upper bound or role check. get_capacity_at_date sums capacity into available FTE; can_pursue_project compares needs vs (capacity - demand) and emits 'GO - Sufficient capacity'.
findings.impact: Staffing/pursuit caller invents hundreds of phantom FTEs so a $100M pursuit that should CAUTION becomes GO — drives understaffed bid/commit decisions.
attack_path: 1) Honest pool (1 PM + 1 superintendent) → can_pursue_project($100M) = CAUTION
findings.remediation: Clamp capacity to sane FTE range (e.g. 0 < capacity ≤ 1.5 per person); require HR/admin role for add_staff; audit phantom headcount vs payroll source of truth.

findings.title: add_risk/import_project_risks accept probability=0 — hide CRITICAL risks from score/VaR/top lists
findings.description: probability is unconstrained. ProjectRisk.__post_init__ sets score=p*impact and level from score; p=0 yields score=0 and LOW even when impact is tens of millions. top_risks sort by score; calculate_var samples with p; expected_loss sums scores.
findings.impact: Project risk submitter zeros probability on material exposures → portfolio expected_loss, VaR, and top_risks omit them while mitigation priorities shift elsewhere.
attack_path: 1) import_project_risks / add_risk with impact=10_000_000, probability=0.8 → CRITICAL
2) Same impact with probability=0.0 → level LOW, score 0
findings.remediation: Require 0 < probability ≤ 1; flag impact-without-probability; separate residual probability from inherent; do not allow submitter to zero portfolio-visible score without review.

findings.title: Unsaniized flight_id path traversal on report write
findings.description: process_survey builds report_path as output_dir / f'{flight.flight_id}_report.json' and opens it for write with no sanitization. flight_id containing ../ escapes the output directory (JSON write is live in the template; ortho/dem paths are string-only).
findings.impact: Survey caller can overwrite arbitrary writable files as the process user with attacker-controlled JSON statistics.
findings.remediation: Allowlist flight_id to [A-Za-z0-9_-]; resolve path and reject if not under output_dir.resolve().
